extracted.intended_audience: attorneys and practitioners who appear before the USPTO; counsel handling USPTO reciprocal disciplinary matters; Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements the USPTO applies when deciding whether to impose reciprocal discipline based on a state disciplinary adjudication under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, including the Selling v. Radford grounds and burden/notice rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO imposition rule under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director shall impose the identical public censure, public reprimand, probation, disbarment, suspension, or disciplinary disqualification unless the practitioner clearly and convincingly demonstrates, and the USPTO Director finds there is a genuine issue of material fact that one of the specified Selling v. Radford grounds applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identical discipline types listed include public censure, public reprimand, probation, disbarment, suspension, disciplinary disqualification. The Director is not reviewing the state proceeding for mere error; the default is to adopt the state's discipline absent narrowly-construed defenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deprivation of due process (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: The procedure elsewhere was so lacking in notice or opportunity to be heard as to constitute deprivation of due process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioner must show by clear and convincing evidence that the prior proceeding's notice or hearing opportunity was so deficient that due process was denied. Mere disagreement with outcome, absence of a single witness, or an unsigned document is insufficient without evidence the practitioner sought continuance, enforcement, or otherwise objected or appealed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infirmity of proof (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: There was such infirmity of proof establishing the conduct as to give rise to the clear conviction that the Office could not, consistently with its duty, accept as final the conclusion on that subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioner must demonstrate substantial defects in the evidence supporting the state finding. Participation in the state hearing, stipulation to facts, or admissions at the state proceeding strongly undermine a claim of infirmity of proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grave injustice (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: The imposition of the same public censure, public reprimand, probation, disbarment, suspension or disciplinary disqualification by the Office would result in a grave injustice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To prevail the practitioner must show the sanction is grossly disproportionate to the misconduct (e.g., conduct not sufficiently grave to warrant the discipline). Arguments that discipline arose from unrelated practice areas, or that it will harm reputation, are insufficient absent showing discordance between misconduct and sanction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument that practitioner was not publicly sanctioned (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any argument that the practitioner was not publicly censured, publicly reprimanded, placed on probation, disbarred, suspended or disciplinarily disqualified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the state action was not actually a public sanction of the types listed, that fact can be pleaded; practitioner must nonetheless prove the absence of the listed public sanction by clear and convincing evidence to avoid reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden and standard of proof: clear and convincing evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The practitioner must clearly and convincingly demonstrate that a genuine issue of material fact exists as to one of the Selling elements; federal/USPTO review uses a narrow standard and the respondent bears the burden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal cases (e.g., In re Kramer; In re Friedman; In re Zdravkovich) hold the practitioner must meet a high evidentiary standard. The USPTO Director will not act as a de novo reviewer to discover errors in the state proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and 40‑day response requirement (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director shall issue a notice directing the practitioner to file a response with the USPTO Director within forty days of the date of the notice establishing a genuine issue of material fact that the imposition of identical discipline would be unwarranted and the reason for that claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice orders the practitioner to present all information they believe sufficient to establish a genuine issue. Practitioners may submit additional information during the forty-day period; failure to file additional evidence after such notice weighs against the practitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misconduct standard under 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6)
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not engage in any conduct that adversely reflects on the practitioner's fitness to practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This regulation provides a basis for USPTO discipline when a practitioner has been publicly reprimanded by a state authority; the Office may impose reciprocal discipline for conduct that reflects adversely on fitness to practice before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of stipulation/admissions and failure to appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner's stipulation to the facts, admission of rule violations, and agreement that a public reprimand was appropriate make it particularly difficult to demonstrate a genuine issue of material fact to avoid reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order emphasizes that admitting facts and agreeing to sanction, and not appealing the state determination, undercuts claims of due process defects, infirmity of proof, or grave injustice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of sanctions subject to reciprocity
rubrics_metrics.description: The types of discipline the USPTO will impose identically under § 11.24 include public censure, public reprimand, probation, disbarment, suspension, and disciplinary disqualification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reciprocal discipline is imposed the USPTO applies the same category of sanction as imposed by the state, absent successful demonstration under the Selling elements.
